about: Wrong answers that point to a specific misunderstanding about linear functions. 'pointsTo' is the subskill to work on. Claude's draft (2026-11-21).

misconceptions.description: Mixes up the input and the output: finds f(11) when asked for the x that gives f(x) = 11.
Drops the minus sign of a negative input (f(−2) worked as f(2)).
Gives the input back instead of the output.
Adds one step of the pattern, however far x jumps.
Divides the change in x by the change in y (run over rise).
Subtracts the y's in one order and the x's in the other, so the sign comes out wrong.
Gives the change in y without dividing by the change in x.
Swaps the slope and the y-intercept.
Drops the sign of the slope or the intercept (y = −2x − 7 has slope 2).
Uses where the line crosses the x-axis as b.
Uses a point's y-value as the y-intercept, when that point isn't on the y-axis.
Thinks a table is linear because y keeps going up, without checking the change is the same each time.
Thinks an equation with x² (or any x) is linear.
Compares only the changes in y when x jumps unevenly (x 0, 1, 3, 4), instead of change in y over change in x.
Doesn't multiply the slope into the second term (y − 4 = 2(x − 1) becomes y − 4 = 2x − 1).
Moves the number on the y side the wrong way (y − 4 = ... becomes y = ... − 4).
Mixes up the intercepts of Ax + By = C (divides by the y number for the x-intercept).
Gives C itself as the intercept, without dividing.
Keeps the x term's sign when moving it across (2x + y = 5 becomes y = 2x + 5).
Solves for y but forgets to divide every term by the number in front of y.
Takes the number in front of x in Ax + By = C as the slope.
Mixes up parallel (same slope) and perpendicular (negative reciprocal).
Flips the slope for a perpendicular line but keeps its sign (2 -> 1/2).
Changes the sign for a perpendicular line but doesn't flip it (2 -> −2).
Keeps the given line's y-intercept instead of finding the new line's from the point.
